title: Hyponatremia that the principal diagnosis excludes as a CC
discharge_summary: SYNTHETIC CASE - NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient: Synthetic Patient 07, 81-year-old female. MRN: SYN-0007
Reason for admission: Weakness, dizziness, and poor oral intake during a heat wave.

She was found to have dry mucous membranes, orthostatic hypotension, and BUN 42 with creatinine 1.0 (her baseline). Sodium was 128 mmol/L on admission. She was treated with IV normal saline at 100 mL/hr, and sodium was checked every 6 hours, rising to 133 on day 2 and 136 at discharge. Hydrochlorothiazide was stopped. Orthostatic symptoms resolved and she was walking independently by day 2.
Discharge plan: Stop hydrochlorothiazide; start amlodipine 5 mg daily. Encourage oral fluids. Basic metabolic panel in 1 week.

expected.notes: Sodium 128 was monitored and treated, so hyponatremia is clinically supported, but E87.1 is a CC that the CMS exclusion list treats as a non-CC when E86.0 is the principal diagnosis. The tool should drop it (no query for CC/MCC purposes).
